docs.title: scfm-benchmark
docs.text:
Donor-aware evaluation of frozen single-cell representations.

The portable demo aligns cells by identity, keeps donor dependency groups intact, fits training-fold probes, and produces donor-level predictions and a report.

git clone https://github.com/xqiu625/scfm-benchmark.git
cd scfm-benchmark
python -m pip install .
scfm-bench demo --out demo-output

Open demo-output/results/report.html. This is a CPU-only synthetic example, not a reproduction of a biological result or a ranking of actual foundation models. The development package is 1.2.0.dev0; no new PyPI release is claimed.

  • CLI and input schema
  • Repository and example output
  • Current research status

The historical research pages are retained below. Their old headline numbers predate the QC rebuild and must not be treated as current evidence. The later scPRINT-2 biological-discovery work remains a separate research workflow.

docs.title: Portable CLI
docs.text: Install the current checkout with python -m pip install . (Python 3.10+).

docs.title: Synthetic demonstration
docs.text:
scfm-bench demo --out demo-output

Produces inputs/*.csv and results/{report.html,metrics.csv,donor_predictions.csv,folds.csv,run.json}. No external data or model downloads. Each output directory must be new.

docs.title: Evaluate frozen representations
docs.text:
scfm-bench benchmark --metadata metadata.csv \
  --embedding model_a=model_a.csv --embedding model_b=model_b.csv \
  --folds 5 --seeds 42 43 44 --out comparison

Metadata requires cell_id,donor_id,cv_group,label. IDs must be non-empty strings; cell IDs must be globally unique. Each donor has one binary label (0/1) and one CV dependency group. Several donors may share a group. Enough groups must contain each label for the requested fold count; one-class train/test folds are refused.

Each representation is a CSV with cell_id and numeric features, containing exactly the metadata's cells. File order may differ. IDs are aligned explicitly; missing/extra/duplicated cells and NaN/Inf features are errors.

Optional --pca NAME=DIMENSIONS fits PCA on the training cells of that named representation. To compare against expression features, supply a separate preprocessed expression-feature CSV; raw-count normalization and feature selection are outside this package. Repeated --embedding and --pca names must be unique.

All representations share donor/group folds. Scaling and probes fit training cells only. Cell predictions are averaged within donor before metrics are computed. Training weights cells equally; metrics weight donors equally. Across-repeat SD is not a confidence interval. Frozen embeddings can still carry upstream leakage or confounding; the tool does not validate their provenance.

docs.title: Historical commands
docs.text: embed, evaluate, diagnose and the old report remain for compatibility. embed/evaluate/diagnose depend on research scripts and HPCC paths outside the wheel; embed may submit SLURM jobs. They are not part of the portable demo. The old report is a file-index renderer; use the report automatically written by demo or benchmark for the new evaluation outputs.

docs.title: scFM Diagnostic Suite
docs.text:
Historical research design, not the portable package's feature list. The old diagnose dispatcher only supports parts of this workflow and requires the HPCC research checkout. Use demo / benchmark for the standalone package.

A three-view methodology for characterising a single-cell foundation model on a clinical task. The three views are deliberately complementary: each isolates one dimension along which a "well-performing" FM can still fail in deployment.

View Question it answers Failure mode it surfaces Adaptation curve How much labelled data does the FM actually need? FM gives no advantage over from-scratch baseline GSEA per-dim What biology do the learned axes encode? FM dimensions encode confounders, not the task SHAP + Jaccard Which genes drive predictions? Do FMs agree? FMs reach the same AUC via incompatible mechanisms

Research implementations live under scripts/. Their inputs and execution requirements differ; the portable package does not unify these three views.

docs.title: 1. Adaptation curve
docs.text:
Code: scripts/29_adaptation_curve/code/adaptation_curve.py

For a target task, train a classifier on (n labelled cells from the target domain) + (all available cells from the source domain), for n ∈ {0, 10, 50, 100, 500, 1000, all}. Repeat with 10 seeds at each n. Compare per-FM curves to a from-scratch PCA-200 + LR baseline.

A useful FM should satisfy both:

  1. Higher Y-intercept (n=0) than from-scratch — i.e., the pre-trained representation transfers without any target-domain labels.
  2. Steeper early slope — i.e., target-domain labels are absorbed faster than they are by a from-scratch baseline.

In our cross-disease test (COVID → sepsis mortality), no FM satisfies both. PCA-200+LR's asymptote (0.964) beats every FM at full data, and only scPRINT-2 beats PCA's Y-intercept (0.920 vs 0.891) — but scPRINT-2 is already flat, so the labelled-data budget is wasted. This is the publishable null finding the field needs to wrestle with.

docs.title: 2. GSEA per-FM dimension
docs.text:
Code: scripts/24_option_c_canonical_input/code/gsea_per_fm_dim.py

Treat each FM embedding dimension as a continuous score per cell. For each dim, rank genes by Pearson correlation with the score and run GSEA against MSigDB Hallmark + KEGG + Reactome. Report the strongest enrichments per dim across all dimensions for each FM.

The result is a two-axis biology for the platelet dataset:

Axis Models Pathways Cytoskeleton / adhesion STATE, UCE, TF Actin, integrin, focal adhesion Translation / coronavirus scPRINT-2, STACK, Geneformer Ribosome, COVID-19 disease

This is how you discover that two FMs achieving the same AUC are using fundamentally different biology to get there.

docs.title: 3. SHAP + Jaccard overlap
docs.text:
Code: scripts/24_option_c_canonical_input/code/per_fm_shap_attribution.py and per_fm_shap_gene_map.py

Train the patient-CV classifier as in evaluate, then run SHAP on the trained model to get per-feature (per-dim) importance. Map dim-level importance back to genes via the GSEA correlation table (view 2). Take the top-k genes per FM and compute pairwise Jaccard overlap.

The Jaccard matrix is diagnostic: two FMs in the same biological axis (e.g., STATE and UCE) overlap at 0.4; FMs across the two axes overlap at ≤0.02. High AUC similarity + low Jaccard = the FMs disagree on mechanism — clinically dangerous because failure modes are not correlated, so ensembling cannot save you.

docs.title: Composite verdict
docs.text:
A model passes the suite if it has:

  • adaptation curve dominating from-scratch baseline,
  • a coherent biology in view 2 (not noise / batch confounders),
  • high Jaccard with at least one other model with a different architecture.

On the platelet COVID-mortality task in our paper, no FM passes all three. STATE comes closest. The framework is task-agnostic — point it at your own clinical h5ad and you get the same diagnostic.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Provisional historical results. This page predates the 2026-09 eight-cohort QC rebuild. Do not use these values as current evidence; see ../current-status.md. Regenerate this page after P2/P3 completes.

Headline numbers from the BIB submission (manuscript ~97% complete, May 2026). All AUCs use patient-level StratifiedGroupKFold with Sample_ID (413 unique donors in the COVID cohort).

docs.title: Primary task: in-hospital mortality (binary)
docs.text:
47,808 platelets from 12 cohorts. fatal = 1 (n = 6,237 COVID + 2,613 sepsis) vs survived = 0 (mild + moderate + recovered + severe; severe = ICU-discharged survivor).

Rank Model Binary AUC (LR) LOBO mean AUC 1 STATE 0.825 0.789 — PCA-200 baseline 0.814 — 2 UCE 0.794 0.750 3 Geneformer 0.778 0.730 4 TranscriptFormer 0.776 — 5 scGPT 0.663 0.494

PCA-200 beats 4 of 5 foundation models. Only STATE beats raw expression with PCA. All DeLong pairwise tests significant except TF vs Geneformer.

docs.text: Axis Best model Value Distribution shift (LOBO) STATE 0.789 Gene dropout @ 70% missing UCE 0.0% drop Sample efficiency @ 5% labels UCE -8.5% FP16 quantisation (all) 0% AUC loss, 2× speedup

docs.title: Cross-disease bidirectional transfer
docs.text:
Train COVID-mortality → test sepsis-mortality, and reverse. Same LR hyperplane applied across diseases — a pure test of embedding-space geometry.

Model COVID → Sepsis Sepsis → COVID Pattern STATE 0.800 0.706 Bidirectional generalizer STACK 0.917 0.698 Bidirectional generalizer UCE 0.798 0.514 Forward-only scPRINT-2 0.855 0.543 Forward-only TF 0.775 0.629 Moderate bidirectional Geneformer 0.742 0.581 Weak bidirectional scGPT 0.352 ⚠ 0.555 Anti-correlated (CI [0.22, 0.50])

scGPT systematically inverts mortality prediction sign across diseases, likely because its 512-dim embedding compresses platelet activation — hyper-activated in COVID-fatal but exhausted in sepsis-fatal.

docs.title: Adaptation curve (the null finding)
docs.text:
PCA-200+LR from-scratch vs FMs, varying labelled sepsis cells n added to the COVID training pool. 10 seeds per n, patient-stratified holdout.

Method n=0 (zero-shot) n=100 Asymptote PCA-200+LR 0.891 0.936 0.964 scPRINT-2 0.920 0.931 0.950 STATE 0.882 0.912 0.948 TranscriptFormer 0.811 0.860 0.912 Geneformer 0.804 0.833 0.878 UCE 0.646 0.756 0.876 STACK 0.643 0.887 0.890

No FM has both higher Y-intercept AND steeper early slope than the from-scratch baseline. Only scPRINT-2 beats PCA on the zero-shot intercept, but it is already flat (slope +0.010 to n=100). PCA's asymptote beats every FM at full data.

docs.title: Multimodal fusion (the silver lining)
docs.text: Late-averaging predicted probabilities across all 6 FMs beats any single FM (AUC 0.849 vs STATE's 0.831). Suggests the FMs encode partially non-redundant information — supported by the SHAP-Jaccard mechanism diagnostic showing two distinct biological axes.

docs.title: What this means for the field
docs.text:
1. Patient-level CV must be the floor for any clinical scFM benchmark. Cell-level CV reports AUCs that are 7–17 percentage points inflated.
  2. PCA + LR is a required baseline. Any FM that does not beat PCA on the target task does not justify its computational cost.
  3. High AUC is necessary but not sufficient. Two FMs at the same AUC can encode incompatible biology — verify with the Diagnostic Suite before deploying.
  4. Multimodal fusion is currently the best deployment strategy. No single FM dominates across robustness, calibration, and generalisation.
